claim_text: Excessive intake of preformed vitamin A (retinol and retinyl esters), unlike provitamin A carotenoids such as beta-carotene, can cause congenital birth defects. NIH ODS advises pregnant people to keep preformed vitamin A intake below the applicable upper limit and avoid high-dose supplements containing preformed vitamin A.
health_goal_or_outcome: Avoidance of excessive preformed vitamin A exposure during pregnancy.

population.age_range: Pregnant adolescents and adults; upper limits vary by age.
population.health_status: General pregnancy nutrition context; individual medical indications require clinical assessment.
population.other_context: Differentiate preformed retinol/retinyl esters from provitamin A carotenoids.

ingredient_form_or_preparation: Preformed vitamin A: retinol and retinyl esters; not equivalent to beta-carotene.
comparator: Preformed vitamin A compared with provitamin A carotenoids.
evidence_summary: NIH ODS Pregnancy and Vitamin A fact sheets describe teratogenic risk from excessive preformed vitamin A and age-specific upper limits; beta-carotene does not share the same established reproductive toxicity in the cited source.
limitations: Exact risk depends on form, dose, total intake and life stage.
Do not apply preformed-vitamin-A UL to beta-carotene.
This record does not provide an individualized prenatal supplement dose.
